texts.preamble: Dhananjoy Mahto vs The State Of Jharkhand on 12 August, 2022 Author: Deepak Roshan Bench: Deepak Roshan 1 In The High Court Of Jharkhand At Ranchi Cr. Revision No. 690 of 2004 ------- Dhananjoy Mahto ..... .... Petitioner Versus 1. The State of Jharkhand 2. Din Dayal Singh ..... .... Opposite Parties Coram : Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Deepak Roshan ------- For the Petitioner :Mr. Shubham Mishra, Amicus For the Opposite Party :Mr. Manoj Kumar Mishra, App ......... 09/12.8.2022 Heard learned counsel for the parties.
texts.facts: 3. The prosecution case in short is that when the Food Inspector inspected the shop of the petitioner on 25.10.1989, he found out that the petitioner was running the shop illegally as the validity of the license was only till 31st March, 1988 and it was not renewed. On the basis of the written report, the instant case was registered and after investigation, police submitted charge-sheet. Accordingly, charges were framed against the accused person for which he pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried and finally the petitioner was convicted.
texts.arguments: 4. Learned Amicus submitted that the trial court has failed to take into consideration that all the other prosecution witnesses were accompanied with P.W.1 and as such no independent eye Dhananjoy Mahto vs The State Of Jharkhand on 12 August, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24731900/ 1 witness/villagers were examined which is not tenable in the eye of law and all the prosecution witnesses were highly interested witnesses as they were the part of the investigation team. He further submits that the defence witness No.1 has specifically stated that the shop was closed since 4 years and inspite of the said submission this fact was not relied. Learned Amicus made an alternative prayer for modifying the sentence for the period already undergone as now the petitioner is aged about 69 years and the case is of the year 1989 and he also remained in custody for about 72 days. As such at this stage sending him back to jail even for short period will hamper the entire family; as such some leniency may be granted by modifying the sentence for the period already undergone. 5. Learned counsel for the State supported the judgments and submits that there is no error in the findings given by the courts below. As such, the conviction cannot be [LEAKAGE_MASK], however the sentence may be modified in lieu of fine.
